chokepoint.binary_decision: Exercise or decline the contractual right of first refusal for a covered future onsite generation or power build-out opportunity, beginning April 2028.
chokepoint.post_decision_phrase: exercise or decline its right of first refusal
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The power supplier also receives a contractually specified choice on covered future power opportunities. Non-voting equity alone does not create that choice. Full exercise procedure and exceptions are not established by the public summary.

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: The Ector County AI campus links future power procurement to rights granted to the original supplier, while upfront credit support and delivery conditions remain separate.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The supplier is positioned as a future project owner and holder of expansion rights. The rights come from the DFA, not voting control. The announcement does not prove collateral posting, power delivery, or universal control of the site.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Inspect the promised full contract exhibits for the scope and exercise procedure of the future power rights and for evidence of collateral posting.

verified_facts.claim: September 21st, 2026 announcement followed September 18, 2026 execution of the PPA and concurrent DFA.
TCDC near Odessa, Ector County, is New Era AI infrastructure; company describes AI training and inference workloads.
Luminant has agreed to supply 200 to 207 MW; supply can come from the Odessa plant, other available sources or ERCOT grid.
TCDC PowerCo must provide a $116 million letter of credit within 15 business days of PPA execution, and additional mutually acceptable security up to $82.8 million by delivery.
After delivery begins New Era must cause issuance of 5% non-voting fully diluted equity in the Project Company for the powered portion to Vistra or its designated affiliate.
Starting April 2028, Vistra has a right of first refusal on future onsite generation or power build-out opportunities at the Ector County site.
A separate right of first offer lasts five years from DFA execution for certain proposed power generation and battery storage projects.
The first-refusal right gives Vistra the choice to exercise or decline it for covered opportunities; specific notices, matching periods and exceptions are not supplied in the 8-K summary.
Luminant obligations depend on conditions precedent by December 31, 2027, including execution of Phase 1 substation/equipment purchase agreement.
Company expects power in Q3 2027; expectation is not completed delivery.
The 8-K says full PPA and DFA texts will be filed with the Form 10-Q for the quarter ending September 30, 2026.
These sources do not establish that collateral has been posted or that power has begun flowing; equity is prospective and non-voting, and rights are limited to covered opportunities.
The four-layer structure connects seller supply, buyer security, prospective project equity and future power rights; interpretation does not imply a veto over all site decisions.
